**Finding: Deviation (medium) — Article IV Term, ¶p0049**

**Issue.** The only renewal language in the Agreement gives Licensor a unilateral option to extend for seven years: *"The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor."* There is no Licensee consent right, no non-renewal notice mechanism, no renewal reminder, and no constraint on renewal pricing. A unilateral multi-year extension sits at our walk-away line. It also contradicts Article IV(II)–(III) of the same paragraph, which contemplate extension only "by mutual written [agreement] of the parties" — an internal inconsistency that should be resolved in our favour.

**Related checks.** No fee-escalation or CPI language exists anywhere in the document (search for "increase" returned nothing; fees are a fixed per-trade schedule), so renewal pricing is presently unconstrained.

**Redline (preferred, validated ok:true).** Replaced the 7-year Licensor option with successive 12-month renewal periods, a Licensee right to decline on 30 days' notice, a Licensor renewal/fee-change reminder 60 days out, and a renewal uplift cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

**Negotiation note.** If Licensor resists the mechanics, the clean fallback is to delete the sentence entirely and rely on Article IV(II)–(III) (renewal by mutual written agreement only), which already appears in the document.
